title: Kindergarten at Hardicht's Brewery, learning German, the ice house
summary: His mother worked at a German brewery whose kindergarten taught the children German; they pasted labels on bottles and played dangerously in the ice house.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: then my mother's moved back to E Street, right across from the school, and I started school and learning was something I had to have. I knew I had to have it. I had to have knowledge. I knew that. So I went to kindergarten and kindergarten was nothing for me. I was making rabbits and horses and little--- those blocks. So they took me out of kindergarten and put me in first grade and I was moving beautifully and I'd tie my shoes and fix (inaudible) and be in school on time and everything.

So then this passed on and then later, first and second grades, (inaudible). But my mother was working at a place called Hardicht's Brewery and at that time, there was nobody to take care of me and my brother, so we would -- they had a kindergarten in Hardicht's Brewery (German is) people and they had a school for the help that were working there.
How did they spell their name?
I mean the people who had --

His name was Chris (PHONETIC) or C-r -- C-h-r -- h-i-r-t-c-h. Chris Hartch 's Brewery. I think the beer still is on the market in Washington, D.C. at the present time. And so in this kindergarten, we were learning German.

Because we were playing in German and when we go to school we'd be in English because in Foggy Bottom, everyone was down there and you had the Potomac Indian down there and you had the -- well, you had Italian, you had the underclass white man, because he was poor, and you had -- see, you have some Arabs down there, too. So all right, going to school and then the kindergarten and then they gave us a little job of pasting the label on the bottles, on the (inaudible), and they used to give us a sandwich called Braunswiger (PHONETIC) and you just got touch of light beer a little and we was happy fellows.

See, when we got out of this kindergarten (inaudible) they had a ice house. This was next to the Harditch's Brewery too, it was. So we would--very dangerous We were around five or six, you know. We had a lot of (inaudible), too. And we used to ----those big boys used to tell us. "Now you go in there." We'd go through the holes that push the ice through the slot and they'd chop it up and get it out. Now, after thought if one of there on us, we would have those big pieces of ice stuck in / froze to death, because it was a whole building of this frosted ice.
